name: Bitter Leaf Anthracnose
description: A fungal disease causing dark sunken lesions on bitter leaf stems and leaves. It is spread by rain splash and is most severe during prolonged wet periods. The disease can cause significant leaf loss and stem dieback.
symptoms: Dark brown to black sunken spots on stems
Irregular brown patches with dark borders on leaves
Leaf edges turning brown and scorched-looking
Stems developing cankers that girdle and kill branches
Dieback of shoot tips in severe infections
causes: Fungal spores surviving on plant debris
Spread by rain splash during heavy rains
Wounds from insect feeding or harvesting
Continuous wet weather for extended periods
treatments: Prune and destroy infected stems and branches
Apply copper-based fungicide spray at weekly intervals
Spray carbendazim or mancozeb at first symptoms
Apply neem oil (5ml/L water) as organic preventive
prevention: Avoid working in the field when leaves are wet
Use clean pruning tools disinfected between plants
Remove and destroy crop debris after harvest
